newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens, unaffected by violence.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens, unaffected by violence.

text.p: The Israeli shekel on Thursday weakened against the dollar and basket of foreign currencies following the dollar's rise abroad and trade was not affected by the political unrest, dealers said.
"The market did not react to the political events and the shekel weakened after the dollar rose abroad," said Ilan Raviv at Israel Discount Bank.
In two days of bloody clashes between Israeli troops and Palestinians 33 Palestinians and five Israelis were killed.

"The Bank of Israel had to intervene on a relatively high scale in the market, buying more than $50 million to support the basket. The market will be influenced by the political unrest between Israel and the Palestinians only if foreign investors decide to leave Israel," Raviv said.

The shekel can trade in a band of seven percent above or below a slope designed to devalue the Israeli currency at six percent a year against a basket of currencies representing Israel's main trading partners.
If the shekel-basket exchange rate reaches the lower trading band the central bank intervenes by buying foreign currency.

The representative rate for the dollar was 3.1800 against 3.1710 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.5567 shekels against 3.5541 on Wednesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8795 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8774 on Wednesday and against the mark at 2.0920 shekels per mark against 2.1019 on Wednesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.1800 shekels.
